name: Undertow Drift

stars.name: The Lighthouse
stars.notes: A millisecond-cadence pulsar sweeping the system with a 2.7-second radio pulse; navigators set clocks by it and shields against it.

planets.name: Scour
planets.notes: A glassy, irradiated pebble of a world; the pulsar wind has sandblasted its surface smooth as worn ballast stone.

planets.name: Leadshot
planets.notes: Dense iron-rich rock orbiting inside the radiation belt's edge; automated crawlers strip its regolith for shielding stock.

planets.name: Keelhaul Deep
planets.notes: Metal-mountains world holding the system's richest transuranic veins; mining happens by telepresence from three light-minutes away, and no closer.

planets.name: Graytide
planets.notes: A cratered drift of rock whose orbit measurably decays toward the pulsar; surveyors re-measure it every decade with growing unease.

planets.name: Blackfathom
planets.notes: A dark ice giant's frozen sibling at the system's rim, its nightside glowing faintly under charged-particle bombardment.

anomalies.name: The Undertow
anomalies.notes: A broad tidal shear zone where spacetime strains against the pulsar's spin; ships lose thrust margin as if caught in an ebb current, and two freighters have been dragged sunward to destruction.

asteroid_belts.name: Driftwood Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin ring of irradiated ice shards; the survey guild anchors its listening posts here, safely outside the undertow.

stations.name: Sounding Line Station
stations.notes: A clustered research habitat boring into a shard for shielding; its staff charts the Undertow's boundaries and buries the ones who ignore them.

faction_control.notes: The Guild holds the sole operating charter, granted after its survey flotilla mapped the Undertow; mining consortiums lease access under strict lane discipline.

history: The pulsar was first logged as a lighthouse-like sweep by a passing freighter's radio officer, giving the star its name and the system its first chart.
The Undertow claimed the ore freighters Marrowick and Kindly Gull within a single year, and the Guild's subsequent survey turned a mining claim into a guarded research preserve.
Last spring, Graytide's orbit was found to be decaying faster than any model allows, and the Guild has quietly doubled its measurement cadence.
description: A dead star spins in the dark, flinging a radio beam across Abysmal Shelf every 2.7 seconds like a lighthouse over an ink-black sea. Its planets are stripped things: a glass-smooth cinder, iron rocks, a mountain of metal, and a rimward ice field, all bathed in radiation that forbids anything soft to survive. The whole system reads on sensors as rhythmic, patient, and hostile.

Only the Deep Survey Guild stays, running Sounding Line Station from the Driftwood Belt and escorting telepresence miners who work Keelhaul Deep's riches from a cautious distance. Minimal traffic crosses the system, mostly Guild tenders, licensed ore runners, and the rare physicist chasing pulsar timing data. Everyone files a lane plan; those who don't are why the lane plan exists.

The Undertow remains imperfectly charted, and its boundary markers have been moved inward twice without explanation. Graytide is falling sunward on a schedule no equation reproduces, and some Guild theorists whisper the pulsar is not merely spinning down but leaning. Whatever is dragging the system's ebb, it lies somewhere below the third orbit, and the Guild intends to sound it before it sounds back.
